scenes.tagline: Abandoned PayPal checkouts, won back on WhatsApp.
scenes.tag: Live on PayPal sandbox · AI agent on Claude Haiku 5.5 · WhatsApp
scenes.vo: Hollaback. When a shopper walks away from a PayPal checkout, an AI agent wins them back on WhatsApp, within a minute.

scenes.label: THE PROBLEM
scenes.head:
Her ads were working.
Her buyers weren't paying.

bullets.v: "I have just put off all my campaigns that's doing amazingly well"
"Why would someone … change their mind on paying?"
70% of online shopping carts are abandoned

scenes.vo: In October, a seller in Nigeria posted that her ads were doing amazingly well. Buyers clicked, got to payment, and left. So she switched the ads off. Another seller lost five payments in one day, and asked why anyone changes their mind at the last step. Seven in ten online carts end this way.

scenes.label: THE GAP
scenes.head:
Reminder emails
don't bring them back

bullets.v: 72% more likely to buy where they can message
+29% PayPal sales with Pay Later messaging

scenes.vo: The usual fix, a reminder email, turns about one and a half percent into sales. Shoppers would rather message, and where PayPal Pay Later is offered, PayPal sales rise twenty-nine percent.

scenes.label: WHAT CHANGES
scenes.head:
One script tag.
A PayPal way to finish.
bullets: Notices the walk-away on the PayPal checkout
Confirms with PayPal the order is still unpaid
Answers the real objection, no coupon blasts
Counts it only when PayPal confirms payment

boxes.title: PayPal checkout
boxes.sub: JS SDK v6 + one script tag

diagram.note: Every step is a real PayPal sandbox call.

scenes.vo: Hollaback is one script tag on a PayPal checkout. It notices the walk-away and confirms with PayPal that the order is still unpaid, so nobody who paid gets nagged. Then an agent answers the real objection with a PayPal way to finish, not a coupon blast.

scenes.head: Kicks Lagos: a Lagos sneaker brand selling abroad
scenes.sub: Real PayPal JS SDK v6 checkout on sandbox. The shopper opts in to WhatsApp, opens Pay Later, then closes it.
scenes.vo: Kicks Lagos is a Lagos sneaker brand selling to customers abroad. A shopper opts in to WhatsApp updates, opens PayPal Pay Later, and closes it.

scenes.head: Within a minute, on WhatsApp
scenes.sub: WhatsApp via the Twilio sandbox; in production, the merchant's own number. "Bit pricey rn": offer_pay_later, then Pay in 4 with the PayPal link.
scenes.vo: Thirty seconds later, PayPal confirms the order is still unpaid, so the agent writes. She says it's a bit pricey. The agent checks Pay Later and offers Pay in 4: twenty-two dollars twenty-five today.

scenes.head: She pays in 4 on PayPal
scenes.sub: PayPal sandbox, US buyer account. Order captured, thank-you on WhatsApp.
scenes.vo: She taps the link, logs in to PayPal, picks Pay in 4 and approves. Back on WhatsApp, the thank-you is already waiting.

scenes.head: The merchant sees it land, live
scenes.sub: AG Grid dashboard over server-sent events. Recovered when PayPal's verified webhook arrives.
scenes.vo: On the merchant's dashboard, built on AG Grid, the cart flips to Recovered the moment PayPal's verified webhook lands, and recovered revenue ticks up.

scenes.head: "Just email me the invoice"
scenes.sub: The agent creates and sends a PayPal invoice (Invoicing v2). Paid, then INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID.
scenes.vo: Another shopper just wants an invoice. The agent creates and sends a PayPal invoice, shares the pay link, and when it's paid, the cart counts as recovered.

scenes.head: Every abandoned checkout, by outcome
scenes.sub: AG Grid: grouped by outcome, pinned totals, quick filter, CSV export.
scenes.vo: Every abandoned checkout lands here, grouped by outcome, with totals pinned at the bottom. Search finds any shopper, order or invoice, and the list exports to CSV.

scenes.head: Every PayPal call, on the record
scenes.sub: create_and_send_invoice via the PayPal Agent Toolkit, then INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID, verified with PayPal.
scenes.vo: Each conversation keeps its receipts: every tool the agent called, including invoices created through PayPal's Agent Toolkit, and every webhook, verified with PayPal.

scenes.head: Guardrails live in code, not in the prompt
scenes.sub: Discount cap 10%, once, after Pay Later. Opt-in only. Money moves only through checked tools.
scenes.vo: The model can't give the store away: discounts are capped at ten percent, once, after Pay Later, and only opted-in shoppers are messaged.

scenes.label: BUILT ON
scenes.head: PayPal does the real work
bullets: JS SDK v6: PayPal and Pay Later buttons, Pay in 4 message
Orders v2: create, check unpaid, capture
PayPal Agent Toolkit: invoices, reminders, order checks
Invoicing v2 and webhooks, each signature verified
Claude Haiku 5.5 runs the agent, inside guardrails
Twilio WhatsApp, AG Grid, Render, Neon Postgres
scenes.vo: Under the hood: PayPal's JavaScript SDK version six, Orders, Pay Later, Invoicing and verified webhooks, with the PayPal Agent Toolkit creating and sending the invoices. Claude Haiku runs the agent, AG Grid powers the dashboard, and it all runs on Render.

scenes.label: WHY IT MATTERS
scenes.head:
Every recovery is a sale
that was already lost

bullets.v: Win back checkouts they had written off
More completed payments, Pay Later and invoices
A share of recovered revenue, paid only on success
8 recoveries from a real phone on PayPal sandbox

scenes.vo: Every recovery is a sale that was already lost, completed through PayPal. Merchants pay a share of what's recovered, so they only pay when it works. Eight real-phone recoveries are on record in PayPal sandbox.

scenes.footer: PayPal JS SDK v6 · Orders v2 · Pay Later · Invoicing v2 · Webhooks · Agent Toolkit · AG Grid · Render
scenes.vo: Hollaback. One script tag, and every PayPal merchant could use it tomorrow.
